answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before joining a market, then slash that bond when fraud is proven through a challenge process that checks signed transaction records. The bond is locked for a fixed period, so creating a knoll of disposable accounts across a mesa of markets ties up capital in every one; sybils become costly rather than free, though wealthy attackers can still participate and collusion can weaken detection in a karst of overlapping groups.
